newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India GDRs mixed on low interest.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India GDRs mixed on low interest.

text.p: Indian global depository receipts (GDRs) were mixed on Tuesday, amid patchy buying interest following domestic market losses earlier, traders said.
A trader said GDRs were generally mixed, with a lack of interest seen capping gains.
The market drifted on Monday after Friday's Hindu festival holiday, dealers said.

Investors booked profits in Bombay earlier, after seeing the market struggle for further gains, but a London trader said support was expected at 3,600 points on Bombay's benchmark index, which he said provided an opportunity to buy blue chips.
Reliance shed 50 cents to $16.00/$17.00, and Hindalco added 50 cents to $29.25/30.25.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed up 1.26 percent, or 0.93 points at 74.73, with the premium over the local market at 17.68 percent from 13.87 percent on Monday.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index shed 1.14 percent to 3,725.87.
Taiwanese stocks picked up on Tuesday after easing on Monday from record highs.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index climbed 0.82 percent or 0.90 points to 110.45 with a premium over the local market of 0.56 percent.
Korean stocks ended lower again, and GDRs tracked them to lower levels.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 0.72 points, or 1.23 percent lower at 57.58. The premium over the local market was 45.16 percent.
